newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israeli planes rocket hills south of Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Israeli planes rocket hills south of Beirut.

text.p: Israeli warplanes rocketed Palestinian guerrilla targets in hills south of Beirut on Friday, Palestinian officials said.
Two jets fired two rockets into the Na'ameh hills where the radical Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine-General Command (PFLP-GC) has bases -- 15 km (nine miles) south of Beirut.
There was no immediate word on casualties in the air assault -- the 49th on Lebanon since the beginning of the year.

Earlier, Katyusha rockets slammed into northern Israel, slightly wounding an Israeli woman. Hizbollah (Party of God), the most formidable guerrilla force fighting Israeli occupation of south Lebanon, said it did not fire the rockets.
The attacks on Friday came amid the worst cross-border violence in south Lebanon since Israel's month-long offensive more than a year ago.

Between Monday and Thursday 13 Lebanese -- including seven civilians -- were killed by bombs, Israeli artillery and Israeli rocket attacks. One member of the Israeli-backed South Lebanon Army militia was killed by a bomb and Israeli commandoes killed five members of Hizbollah with a roadside bomb.
